title: Stop-and-substitution / reversal: interface contract for AI video review
note: No film viewed, no AI output evaluated, no model named. Own invented subjects only.

M1_stop_and_substitution.description: Camera stops; every subject not leaving holds the position the last exposure caught; leaving subject slips out; substitute or returning subject steps in; camera restarts.
M1_stop_and_substitution.key_invariant: Position of all non-leaving subjects is frozen at stop; any deviation is the failure signature.
M1_stop_and_substitution.ai_analogy: A generative cut between two prompts or scenes; the model does not enforce the hold-position invariant automatically.

M2_reversal.description: Natural action photographed forward; film threaded so last frame plays first (projector route), or film run backward through camera (camera route). The worked example wording differs between line 8139 (camera) and caption lines 8078-8079 (projector); which route a given AI tool uses is not stated here.
M2_reversal.key_invariant: Motion direction is inverted across all frames; partial inversion is the failure signature.

input.subject_count: integer — number of subjects in scene at stop

output.checkpoints_applicable: array of checkpoint IDs from the checkpoints block below
output.cannot_check: list of things that cannot be verified at the given review_unit

checkpoints.when: intended_effect is substitution, disappearance, or return
checkpoints.question: Do all non-leaving subjects maintain the same position across the cut frame? Any drift is a failure of the hold-position invariant.
Does the substitute figure appear at the correct position (where the original was last exposed) rather than at an interpolated or drifted position?
Does motion run opposite to the natural direction across the full clip? Check start and end frames; partial reversal (some frames forward, some backward) is the failure signature.
Is the reversal applied to the full sequence, or only to a segment? The book describes full-film reversal; partial reversal is not described there and would need separate justification.

explicit_gaps: The book does not say how many frames constitute a 'clean' cut; no minimum frame count is given.
Which reversal route an AI video tool uses (frame-reorder vs. temporal-inversion in latent space) is not addressed by the book and not established here.
The hold-position invariant assumes discrete stop points; AI interpolation between keyframes may produce a continuous drift that has no direct analog in the book.
The worked example wording disagreement (camera line 8139 vs. projector caption lines 8078-8079) is noted but not resolved; no determination is made here.
No audio claim: the book's stop mechanism applies to the visual track only; sound handling is not addressed.
